<!-- Generated by codeflower-app's cmd/gendocs: do not edit. -->

Stop the code flower client running for the config directory, whether it runs in a window or in the background (as "codeflower tunnel", "sandbox" and "run" start it). Paired browsers lose remote access until a client runs again.

The sandboxes the client started from its page stop with it: as when quitting from the page, their working chats are first asked to save their work and wrap up, and each sandbox stops when they are done, at most after 10 minutes ("client: &#123;wrap_up_minutes: N&#125;"). Ctrl+C, or --now, stops them at once.

Sandboxes merely connected to it keep running: those started in a terminal ("codeflower sandbox", "codeflower run"), by a batch job, or added by their address. With no client running, it does nothing.


## Usage

```sh
codeflower client stop [flags]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config string` |  | config directory of the client (or set $CODEFLOWER_CONFIG; default ~/.codeflower) |
| `--now` |  | stop the sandboxes it started at once, without asking their chats to wrap up |
